title: Country‐Scale Isoscapes of Leaf Carbon and Nitrogen of Brazilian Tree Species
content:
Abstract

Stable carbon and nitrogen isotope compositions of plant leaves provide insights into interactions between vegetation and its environment. In C3 plants, preferential assimilation of 12C over 13C during photosynthesis produces a measurable foliar δ 13C signal. Comparing foliar δ 13C with atmospheric δ 13C allows carbon isotope discrimination (Δ13C) to be quantified. Foliar δ 15N, in turn, reflects nitrogen sources, transformations, and plant uptake. However, tropical regions remain underrepresented in global isotope data sets. Here, we developed country-scale isoscapes of Δ13C and bulk foliar δ 15N for C3 trees across Brazil at 1-km resolution. We analyzed approximately 6,440 leaf samples grouped into 188 georeferenced clusters across major Brazilian biomes. Climate, soil, and vegetation covariates were used to perform regression kriging (RK) and random forest (RF) modeling approaches. RF outperformed RK for Δ13C and showed comparable performance for δ 15N, yielding cross-validated R 2 values of 0.47 and 0.51, respectively. Key predictors of Δ13C included precipitation of the wettest quarter, aridity, vapor pressure, relative humidity, and soil pH. The most important predictors of foliar δ 15N were mean annual precipitation, precipitation of the wettest month, potential evapotranspiration, relative humidity, and soil δ 15N. The isoscapes reveal spatial gradients consistent with ecological and physiological expectations and constitute the first country-scale framework for foliar isotope variation in Brazil. They provide spatial baselines for evaluating carbon─water interactions and nitrogen cycling in land-surface and Earth system models, and may also support applications in wildlife forensics and the provenance assessment of plant-derived products.
